newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran sets up tents for quake refugees.
newsitem.headline: Iran sets up tents for quake refugees.

text.p: Iranian relief teams have set up 5,248 tents to shelter families made homeless by two earthquakes that hit the country's mountainous northeast this week, the Iranian news agency said on Saturday.

Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS) teams erected the tents in the quake-striken regions of Bojnurd and Shirvan, it said. They distributed 1.2 million litres of fuel, food, blankets, heaters, clothes, shoes and other relief supplies.
Hamid Mahalati, managing director of IRCS operations in the region, said 3,800 families were living in tents, schools and sport facilities after Tuesday's earthquakes made 25,000 people homeless.

Officials said on Thursday at least 79 people were killed and 260 injured in the tremors, measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale. Since then, there have been 420 aftershocks, the strongest measuring 4.3. Some 65 villages were damaged.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in a densly populated area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
